lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: And you, Callidemides? How did you die? You know my story—I was a parasite at Dinias's table, stuffed myself, and choked to death. You were there.

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: I was there, Zenophantus. My death, however, was something of a surprise. You know old Ptoeodorus, I suppose?

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: The rich old man with no kids? The one you spent all your time hovering around?

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: That's the one. I waited on him hand and foot because he kept promising to make me his heir. But the thing was dragging on forever—the old man was outliving Tithonus—so I figured out a shortcut to the inheritance. I bought some poison and made a deal with his cupbearer: as soon as Ptoeodorus asked for a drink—and he likes it strong—the boy was to have the poison already mixed in a cup and hand it to him. If he did this, I swore I'd set him free.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: So what happened? It sounds like there's quite a twist coming.

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: Well, we had just come back from the baths. The boy had the two cups ready—the one with the poison for Ptoeodorus, the other for me. Somehow he blundered. He gave the poisoned cup to me, and the safe one to Ptoeodorus. The old man took a drink, and I instantly stretched out flat on the floor—a substitute corpse! [pause] Why are you laughing, Zenophantus? You really shouldn't laugh at a friend.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: [laughs] Because it's hilarious, Callidemides! What did the old man do?

lines.speaker: Callidemides
lines.text: At first he was a bit startled by how sudden it was. Then, I suppose, he figured out what had happened, and he started laughing too at the cupbearer's mistake.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: Well, you really shouldn't have taken the shortcut. The main road would have gotten you there safely enough, even if it took a little longer.
